chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Al-Nawfali, from Al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

Ja'far ibn Abi Talib was in the presence of the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family). A quince was gifted to the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family), so the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) cut a piece from it and handed it to Ja'far. He refused to eat it, so he said: 'Take it and eat it, for it purifies the heart and emboldens the timid.'
And in another report: 'Eat it, for it clears the complexion and improves the offspring.'
ai.seo_question: What are the spiritual and physical benefits of eating quince according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Recorded in Al-Kafi, this narration highlights the Prophet’s (peace be upon him) practical wisdom in using quince (safarjal) for both spiritual and physical well-being, linking its consumption to the purification of the heart (tathkir al-qalb) and the strengthening of courage. The variant reading emphasizing the beautification of offspring reflects the Shia tradition’s holistic view of health, where dietary habits are seen as integral to nurturing the next generation's physical and moral character.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Al Nowfaly, from Al Sakuny, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> Bin Abu Talib<sup>as</sup> was in the presence of the Prophet<sup>saww</sup> and he<sup>as</sup> gifted a Quince to the Prophet<sup>saww</sup>. So the Prophet<sup>saww</sup> cut off a piece from it and gave it to Ja’far<sup>as</sup>, but he<sup>as</sup> refused to eat it (out of respect). So he<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘Take it, and eat it, for it purifies the heart, and emboldens the timid’.
And in another report: ‘(He<sup>saww</sup> said): ‘Eat, for it clears the colour and improves the child birth’.
en.sarwar: 2. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from al-Nawfaliy from al-Sakuniy who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said that

Ja‘far ibn abu Talib was with the Holy Prophet, O Allah, grant compensation to Muhammad and his family worthy of their services to Your cause, and he presented quince to the Holy Prophet. The Holy Prophet cut one piece from it and gave it to Ja‘far but he declined to eat it. The Holy Prophet said, ‘Take and eat it. It makes the heart (mind) intelligent and emboldens a coward heart.’
In another Hadith it is said, ‘Eat it; it clears the color and beautifies the child (to be born).”’
